Control statement: Security roles are documented. The owner holds every operating role, and users' own responsibilities (complementary user entity controls) are written down.

Control statement: Sign-in tokens last 1 hour and refresh tokens 30 days. The owner can sign a user out of every device.

Control statement: Every quarter the owner reviews every account that can reach the system (app users, AWS identities, code-host access and connected apps) against the people who should have access, and records the result.

Control statement: GitHub Actions deploys through OIDC federation: only the main branch of the app repository can assume the deploy role, sessions last 1 hour, and no AWS keys are stored in GitHub. Pull-request CI gets no AWS access.

Control statement: Recovery of administrator access from a new device is tested and recorded, and printed break-glass recovery codes are kept offline.

Control statement: Every API route requires a valid sign-in token. The function takes the user ID only from the verified token, never from the request, and every read and write is limited to that user's partition.
The app repository is private with the owner as its only member, and workflows get the least permissions they need.

Control statement: All data elements are listed with their classification, location and owner, and the inventory is updated when a feature adds new data.

Control statement: User content is encrypted on the user's device before it leaves it: AES-256-GCM, a fresh random IV per record, and the user ID plus record key bound in as additional data. The data key is wrapped by a passphrase key (PBKDF2-SHA256, 600,000 iterations) and a recovery-code key. The server, the owner and AWS hold only ciphertext.
Notes: Compensating control: makes customer-managed server keys (SC-12/SC-28) add little, and limits most server-side breaches to metadata and availability. Does not protect against a changed app (R-02, R-04)

Control statement: When a user sets a data passphrase, the app blocks common passphrases and encourages several words, with a self-hosted check and no third-party scripts.
Evidence: Planned: app change. Today: length check only, tracker@4af3f74:web/js/app.js:42

Control: Provider encryption in transit and at rest
Control statement: All traffic uses HTTPS (HTTP redirects, HSTS for one year, TLS required on the bucket). Stored files and table data are encrypted at rest by AWS.
Evidence: tracker@4af3f74:infra/lib/tracker-stack.ts:228-229, 253, 269, 276. Table encryption at rest is an AWS default (relied on, VND-02)
Notes: AWS-managed keys only, by decision D-020. Customer-managed KMS keys aren't used, because DAT-02 already makes the stored data ciphertext

Control statement: Record names are changed so stored keys no longer reveal which days a user logged something. Only sync timestamps remain visible.
A retention schedule sets how long each kind of data and backup is kept, why, and how it's deleted, including whether the 3-year backup copy is needed. Users are told plainly.
Notes: Phase 6 deliverable

Control: Pull request with self-review for every change
Control statement: Every change to the app goes through a branch and a pull request with a self-review checklist. The merged pull request is the change approval record, and rollback is a revert.
Evidence: tracker@4af3f74:.github/pull_request_template.md:5-12; every change since 2026-10-31 merged by pull request (app PRs #1, #4, #6, #7)
Notes: Not enforced by branch protection (a paid feature for private repositories), so the process depends on the owner following it. Phase 8 tests whether every deploy had a PR

Control: Automated checks on every pull request
Control statement: CI runs the unit tests, type check and an offline infrastructure build on every pull request before merge, with no AWS access.
Notes: Advisory: a red check doesn't technically block a merge (no branch protection)

Control statement: Production changes only through the pipeline, from main. Tests and checks run again before deploy, and deploys never run at the same time.
Notes: A manual CloudShell deploy is documented as a fallback (DEPLOY.md). It should be recorded if ever used

Control statement: All app resources are defined in one CDK stack, so the configuration baseline is the code at a given commit and changes go through CHG-01.
Notes: Exceptions outside the code: the backup copy vault (BCK-03) and account-level settings (VUL-03)

Control statement: The owner receives an email for every production deploy, so a deploy the owner didn't make gets noticed.
Every production deploy is listed in a changelog users can read, so a change to the code that handles passphrases is visible to them, not only to the owner.
Notes: Detective control for an accepted risk

Control statement: The app uses no third-party scripts or frameworks, builds the page without innerHTML, and the API never trusts a user ID from the request.
Notes: Written as a coding standard in Phase 3

Control: Content Security Policy and security headers
Control statement: A strict Content Security Policy allows scripts, styles and connections only from the app's own origin and the sign-in service, with no inline scripts. Framing is blocked, MIME sniffing is off, no referrer is sent, and camera, microphone and location are disabled.
The Content Security Policy also requires Trusted Types, so the browser blocks unsafe writes to the page.
The API checks the format of every record key, limits the size of each record and the number per request, and refuses to delete the keyring.

Control: Authorization tests on every API route
Control statement: Automated tests check, on every pull request and deploy, that no API route lets one user read, change or delete another user's records.
Evidence: tracker@4af3f74:infra/test/api.test.mjs:18, 28, 35, 43, 54 (all four routes, plus no-token access on every route)

Control statement: Tests and CI use made-up data and a dummy account. Real user data is never used for testing, and the demo uses fake sample data in the browser only.
Notes: No separate staging environment. A documented limitation for a one-person service; CI and offline synth stand in for it

Control statement: Dependencies install exactly from the lockfile, with install scripts off and before any AWS access exists. GitHub Actions are pinned to commit SHAs, and AWS credentials are given only to the deploy step.
Dependabot opens monthly update pull requests that must pass CI, and security alerts are on. The owner reviews alerts and update PRs every month.

Control statement: Scheduled read-only checks test the AWS account against the control set (MFA, public access, encryption, logging, backups, domain settings) and keep timestamped evidence.

Control statement: The domain's transfer lock, auto-renew, contact details and renewal payment are checked and kept on.
